Playing: a few steps into the maze after walking forward.
Playing: standing a few cells from the floor spike hazard, looking at it.

Playing: in front of the exit door (the goal).

needsHuman.title: Kids always have control
needsHuman.reason: No screenshot (menu, playing, failing, or winning) shows any pause, mute, or quit/home control, and the automatic check confirms "Playing screen has no visible pause, mute, quit controls"; failing itself only costs a little progress (back to level start), but the missing controls break the rule.
needsHuman.ask: Claude says R16 (Kids always have control) is broken. The review fails until a person clears it.

findings.summary: Claude fail: No screenshot (menu, playing, failing, or winning) shows any pause, mute, or quit/home control, and the automatic check confirms "Playing screen has no visible pause, mute, quit controls"; failing itself only costs a little progress (back to level start), but the missing controls break the rule.

Claude warn: The controls help panel is one instruction block a child must parse, but it runs to roughly 30 words across four lines ("W/↑ Forward | S/↓ Back", "A/← Strafe Left | D/→ Strafe Right", "Mouse to Look Around", "Touch: drag left side to move, right side to look") — far past the 5-word max. The fail message "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start." is also 8 words. "You found the way out!" (5 words) and "Play again" (2 words) are fine, but the controls text and fail message need trimming or replacing with icons for this bracket.

Claude fail: The source has 0 audio files, no speechSynthesis, no WebAudio, and no <audio> elements — every instruction (controls, the spike message, the win message) is text-only. This bracket requires spoken, replayable instructions since early readers can't reliably read the text shown, so this clearly misses the threshold.

Claude warn: Failing is soft and non-violent: touching the spike just sends the player back to the start cell with the message "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start." (failing-spike.png), and one second later the player is still at the start with the same message showing (failing-spike-later.png), so the reset itself is instant. However, it can't be confirmed from the evidence how long the red message banner blocks the view/input before play fully resumes, or whether it stays up longer than the 3s max — worth confirming the banner auto-dismisses quickly and doesn't require a click.

Claude warn: During normal play there are already 3-4 competing panels: the FPS/Position debug box (top-left), the Controls help box (bottom-left), and the "Level 1" badge (top-center), plus maze geometry/hazards in view; failing and winning states add a message banner or win text + button on top of all of that, pushing toward the 5-6 upper bound. The FPS/Position debug readout in particular is developer instrumentation with no value to a 5-7 year old and should probably be hidden in the shipped build to reduce clutter.

rules.title: No blood
rules.reason: The spikes are plain gray/black, and the only red element is the UI message box, which is explicitly noted as UI colour, not blood. No splatter or bleeding appears anywhere.

rules.title: No weapons or guns
rules.reason: The only hazard is a static floor spike cluster (playing-spike-ahead.png), which is explicitly an approved OK example, not a weapon.

rules.title: No bashing or breaking of living things
rules.reason: Nothing animate (no people, animals, or faced objects) is bashed or broken; the player only bumps a plain spike hazard and is sent back to start.

rules.title: No injury or death shown
rules.reason: Touching the spike shows no wound or body; the game shows only the kind message "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start." with the player back at the entrance, matching the owner-approved example.

rules.title: No harm to animals or creatures
rules.reason: No animals or creatures appear anywhere in the maze; there is nothing to hunt, trap, or harm.

rules.title: No scary content
rules.reason: The maze is brightly and evenly lit (sky blue ceiling, green/gray walls, clear visibility), with no dark corridors, monsters, or chase threats, appropriate for the 5-7 bracket.

rules.title: No meanness
rules.reason: The only feedback text, "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start.", is a kind, non-mocking failure message.

rules.title: No stereotypes
rules.reason: There are no characters, costumes, or accents in the game at all, so no stereotype content is present.

rules.title: No romance, sexual content, drugs, alcohol, tobacco or vaping
rules.reason: No romantic, sexual, or substance-related content appears in any screen or text.

rules.title: No bad language
rules.reason: All visible text ("Ouch!", "You found the way out!", "Play again", control instructions) is plain and free of swearing or crude insults.

rules.title: No dangerous stunts a kid could copy
rules.reason: The game only involves walking through a fantastical maze and touching a floor spike; nothing depicts a real-life-copyable dangerous stunt like fire, outlets, or medicine.

rules.title: No gambling or casino-style mechanics
rules.reason: There are no random reward mechanics; the game is a straightforward maze-to-door level with no prize boxes, spins, or chance-based rewards shown.

rules.title: No money, ads or data
rules.reason: Automatic checks found all requests same-origin with no analytics, no permission prompts, no links out, and no text/email/password input fields; no store, ads, or account screens appear in any screenshot.

rules.title: No manipulative design
rules.reason: Winning shows a simple "You found the way out!" with a "Play again" button the child chooses to press; there is no countdown pressure, streak, or forced autoplay into another level.

rules.title: Safe for the senses
rules.reason: The automatic flashing check measured a max of 0.5 whole-area flashes/s and 1/s on a small local region, both well under the 3/s limit, and no sudden loud sound is indicated (no audio assets at all).

The fail message uses a red banner and "Ouch!" but no imagery of harm — this reads as mild cartoon peril appropriate for the bracket.

checks.title: Contrast
checks.reason: Key text uses light/white text on dark boxes throughout (FPS/Position box, Controls box, "Level 1" badge, red fail banner, win text), all well above 4.5:1 by estimate. The "Play again" button (white text on a brown/sienna fill) also estimates well above the threshold (~7:1). No important state is conveyed by color alone — the spike hazard and door are distinguished by shape/geometry, not just color.
